ai.prompt: I'm looking at the Solaris UI documentation for {{component}} ({{url}}). Help me understand how to use it. Be ready to explain concepts, give examples, or help debug based on it.

basic.note: Identity column with sticky first cell, grade columns with maxima, and footer averages.

breakdown.note: MP combines FT+AT, GS1 and GS2; “+” opens a dialog with the parts and the result.

composed.note: Pagination is projected into the table footer slot, so it shares the gradebook border.

gradebook.description: Grade matrix with semester groups, result badges, and inline grade editing.

bulk.hint: Select rows, enter the grade, and apply it in bulk. You can also paste an Excel column straight into the editor.

editing.note: Enter or double-click a grade to edit; committing updates the rows owned by the consumer. With multiple selection use bulk commit; with paste enabled you can paste values from Excel.

examples.note: Start with the default gradebook, then explore semesters, editing, and server data below.

hint.gs1: Global Solution, project grade up to 20 points.
hint.gs2: Second-semester Global Solution, project grade up to 20 points.

installation.note: Install the single Solaris package, then import the component.

layout.label: Column layout
layout.note: Auto sizes columns to content. Full width distributes them across the container.

legend.label: Result legend
legend.note: A dotted legend explains result and status badges at a glance.

scales.label: Grade scale
scales.note: Switch the grade scale; formatting, parsing, and sorting follow the active scale.

semesters.note: Consecutive grade columns merge under semester groups (1st and 2nd); the result group carries MP and SITUAÇÃO. Use the tabs to pin the first column, both edges, or none.

scroll.hint: Scroll the table sideways to see the sticky columns in action.

server.note: A simulated server owns rows, total, and loading through SolarisTableDataSource.

statuses.note: Each cell carries a status (graded, late, missing, excused) with a subtle dot next to the number and a screen-reader label; never color-only.

gradebook.title: Gradebook

totals.note: The footer can be computed inside the gradebook with aggregate (average, sum, min, max, median, or weighted); an explicit footerValueOf always wins. The MP column is computed per row from GS1 and GS2, with no typing. Enable the MÁX columns and switch rounding to see the footer effect.
